title: Viva Insights: Copilot Studio agents report adds autonomous agents and time and cost savings
summary: Hold: the Graph role requirement omits the distinction between delegated and application access, potentially sending administrators to assign an unnecessary privileged role. The report coverage, licensing, data-sharing controls and deletion script are supported; the conflicting Microsoft descriptions of autonomous-agent coverage are correctly disclosed.

claims.claim: The change adds autonomous-agent adoption and time and cost savings to the Copilot Studio agents report.
claims.quote: Enhancement to Copilot studio agents report (Viva Insights) - 1. Inclusion of agents with "generative" orchestration 2. Autonomous agent adoption and impact (maker led time and cost saving).

claims.claim: The report is a Power BI template in Viva Insights advanced analysis.
claims.quote: In the Viva Insights analyst experience, select Create analysis. Under Power BI templates, navigate to Copilot Studio agents report and select Set up analysis.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report now covers autonomous as well as conversational agents.
claims.quote: The card on the left shows the Agent landscape as the total number of agents within the tenant, split by conversational and autonomous agents.

claims.claim: Autonomous Agent Impact shows sessions over time.
claims.quote: The chart on the left shows the number of sessions over time

claims.claim: Autonomous Agent Impact shows successful and unsuccessful session outcomes.
claims.quote: you can toggle between this and agent session outcomes based on successful and unsuccessful outcomes.

claims.claim: Autonomous Agent Impact shows average completion time.
claims.quote: The chart in the center of the page highlights the average completion time for the selected timeframe

claims.claim: Autonomous Agent Impact shows sessions per trigger.
claims.quote: The chart on the right shows the number of sessions per trigger for the agent in the selected timeframe

claims.claim: Autonomous Agent Impact offers sessions per action.
claims.quote: as well as the option to select the number of sessions per action for the agent in the selected time frame

claims.claim: Autonomous Agent Impact includes estimated agent assisted impact.
claims.quote: the Estimated agent assisted impact, which reflects the cumulative Agent Assisted Hours (AAH) that might be achieved through the deployment of the autonomous agent.

claims.claim: The report defines autonomous agents as agents built in Copilot Studio with defined event triggers.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents are agents built in Copilot Studio with defined event triggers.

claims.claim: The February 24, 2026 release notes announce autonomous agents with generative orchestration and adoption, time-saved and cost-benefit metrics.
claims.quote: February 24, 2026 ... What changed: The agent report now includes autonomous agents with generative orchestration. It also offers new metrics related to adoption, time saved, and cost benefits.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Maker-led savings inputs from Copilot Studio are passed to Viva Insights.
claims.quote: Maker-led inputs: Maker-led inputs are passed to Viva Insights and Viva Insights reflects the updated value.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Maker-led savings values cannot be edited in Viva Insights.
claims.quote: Maker-led values are not editable in Viva Insights.

claims.claim: Inferred autonomous-agent hours include knowledge-source reference counts multiplied by a research-based six-minute default.
claims.quote: This is estimated by multiplying the number of times knowledge sources were referenced with the information retrieval time savings multiplier, which is six minutes.

claims.claim: Inferred autonomous-agent hours include actions performed multiplied by the time savings multiplier for each action type.
claims.quote: Time saved in performing actions: This is estimated by multiplying the number of times an action was performed by an agent, multiplied by the time savings multiplier for that particular action type.

claims.claim: The formula uses an approximately 2.8-minute generic multiplier for successful sessions without independent actions.
claims.quote: Number of successful sessions without presence of independent actions x TimeSavings_Generic (in minutes) ... The generic time savings multiplier (TimeSavings_Generic) is about 2.8 minutes

claims.claim: Agent assisted impact cost is estimated by multiplying agent assisted hours by an average hourly rate.
claims.quote: This is an estimate of the value of an agent's impact over the given time period, calculated by multiplying Agent assisted hours by an average hourly rate.

claims.claim: The default hourly rate is $72, based on U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data.
claims.quote: By default, this hourly rate is set to $72, based on data compiled by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

claims.quote: If you change the value, it updates the value for that particular agent. You can't use the calculator for maker-led inputs.

claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the report reads metrics and takes no action on agents' with 'The report shows agent adoption and impact metrics.' The sources describe reporting, but do not explicitly state that no action on agents is possible.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The Graph call needs Privileged Role Administrator at least, without qualifying the authentication type.
claims.quote: Application | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory ... For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role ... Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.
claims.fix: Replace the Graph role requirement in controls[2].note, its table note and Governance controls prose with: 'For delegated Graph access using work or school accounts, Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged supported role, or a custom role can grant the required permissions. Application access requires RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory application permission.' Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/rbacapplication-post-roleassignments?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: An admin UI for deleting all Copilot Studio agents data held in Viva Insights is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Viva Insights delete Copilot Studio agents data admin center user interface deletion'; opened delete-copilot-studio-agents-data and the report page. The workflow deletes through PowerShell; Entra UI steps register and consent to an app, not delete report data.

claims.claim: The documented deletion script call is .\CopilotAgentsDelete.ps1 -[ClientId] -[TenantId].
claims.quote: Run the script using the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID you saved: .\CopilotAgentsDelete.ps1 -[ClientId] -[TenantId]

claims.claim: The deletion feature is public preview.
claims.quote: This feature is for public preview customers only. Features in preview might not be complete and could undergo changes before becoming available in the broader release.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights Administrator runs the deletion script.
claims.quote: The Viva Insights Administrator runs a PowerShell cmdlet to delete Copilot Studio agents data in Viva Insights.

claims.claim: Deletion uses a registered app with AdministratorSettings.ReadWrite permission.
claims.quote: Select Workplace Analytics and select Delegated permissions. Under Select permissions, select AdministratorSettings.ReadWrite.

claims.claim: Deletion is irreversible and the data cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: If you delete Copilot Studio agents data, the data can't be recovered. ... You can't un-do this deletion.

claims.claim: Earlier query results become unavailable after deletion.
claims.quote: Queries you ran before you deleted Copilot Studio agents data are also no longer available to analysts.

claims.claim: After deletion, new queries cannot run for one month.
claims.quote: After the data is deleted, the query won't auto-refresh, and you can't run any new queries for one month.

claims.claim: The environment data-sharing and cross-geo settings can also be controlled for environment groups.
claims.quote: Sharing Copilot Studio agent data with Viva Insights ... You can also control this setting for environment groups. ... Cross-geo boundary sharing ... You can also control this setting for environment groups.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no setting that excludes only autonomous agents from this report as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Viva Insights Copilot Studio agents report exclude only autonomous agents data sharing setting'; opened settings-features, analytics-viva-insights and the report. Query filters select named agents, surfaces and types; no autonomous-only reporting exclusion switch was documented.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to set local hourly rates and time multipliers and enter maker-led savings, but these controls have no table rows.
claims.quote: Agree a local hourly rate and time multipliers with finance ... Ask makers of key autonomous agents to enter maker-led savings ... controls: data sharing, cross-geo sharing, Insights Analyst role, deletion.
claims.fix: Remove the two At rollout checklist bullets beginning 'Agree a local hourly rate and time multipliers' and 'Ask makers of key autonomous agents to enter maker-led savings'. Their controls have no rows; this correction does not add rows. The existing body explanation can remain.

claims.claim: Action review is assigned although the launched report enhancement and its data flow arrive without an administrator choosing the change.
claims.quote: action: review; defaultState: on; summary: no admin action is needed if the data feed is already on. The standard defines review as an optional capability or new control that changes nothing until an admin or maker chooses it.
claims.fix: Change action from 'review' to 'prepare': the report enhancement arrives on the existing data feed, and the low-risk, low-cost response is communication and checking existing reporting choices, not enabling an optional new capability.
